observation.visible_scene: A close-up, dimly lit view of an oil/kerosene lantern's burner assembly: a perforated metal ring surrounds a central wick holder, enclosed by a glass globe, with a thin dark wire guard crossing the frame diagonally. A bright yellow-orange flame with a faint blue base burns at the center throughout the excerpt. As the clip progresses the framing widens/tilts downward, revealing the dark metal fuel-tank/base of the lantern and, in the later frames, a person's finger/hand entering at the lower-left edge.
visible_changes: The flame is present and burning in every sampled frame, its shape and tilt flickering slightly (more vertical in some frames, leaning in others) without going out.

The camera view gradually pulls back and shifts downward: early frames are tightly cropped on the perforated ring and flame, while later frames include more of the lantern's lower metal body and a curved guard wire at the bottom of the globe.
A fingertip/hand becomes visible at the lower-left corner starting around the middle-to-late portion of the excerpt and remains there through the final frames, positioned near the lantern base.
The apparent angle of the diagonal wire relative to the flame changes between frames, consistent with the shifting viewpoint rather than the wire itself moving independently.
The perforated ring and central burner stay roughly centered relative to each other across the clip, indicating the lantern body is largely stationary while the framing changes.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the hand/finger is doing to the lantern (holding, adjusting the wick, or merely resting) is not shown.
Whether the flame was just lit or has been burning before the excerpt, and whether it continues unchanged afterward.
The cause of the framing change (camera movement vs. the lantern being moved) cannot be confirmed from background evidence.
uncertain_details: The exact orientation changes of the flame are hard to separate into true flicker versus parallax from the moving viewpoint.
It is unclear whether the diagonal wire is part of a fixed guard or a separate tool/object, as only its silhouette is visible.
The degree of camera zoom versus pan/tilt is uncertain given the close, low-contrast framing.
